tweets: NAD+ precursors (oral) vs. injections — what human trials actually show. Not rodent studies, not cell cultures. Here's the breakdown:
Most human data on NAD+ precursors comes from oral forms (NR/NMN). Effects are measurable but modest — typical of nutrient repletion, not transformative change.
Injectable NAD+ has far less human data. What exists is mostly small, uncontrolled studies. Some show acute effects, but durability and safety aren't well mapped.
Key gap: no head-to-head trials comparing equivalent doses of oral vs. injectable NAD+ precursors in humans. All comparisons are indirect.
Biggest NAD+ injection studies focus on addiction recovery (not longevity/optimization). Effects there may not translate to healthy users.
Bottom line: injectable NAD+ is a clinical tool, not a biohack. It's physician-supervised for a reason — we don't yet have clean data on ideal use cases or dosing.
